title: Learned Holter analysis agrees with physician AF-burden estimates
summary: A trained ECG-analysis system estimated atrial-fibrillation burden in seven-day recordings. In 47 recordings with intermediate burden, correlation with physician review was 0.998 and agreement bias was −0.006. This validates measurement agreement in a selected cohort, not treatment or outcome benefit.
organization: University Hospital Basel; University of Basel

evidence.tested: 100 recordings from82 patients;53 zero/full-burden recordings were separated from the47 intermediate-burden comparisons. Repeated recordings were assessed with a patient-random-intercept sensitivity analysis.
evidence.unknown: Small sample and few women limit transfer. Paced rhythms were excluded. Training architecture and training/test overlap were not fully documented in the study; no efficiency or clinical-outcome benefit measured.
evidence.ai_role: Previously trained algorithms classify ECG rhythm and aggregate detected AF duration into burden.

source_review.scope: Primary indexed clinical/reference/software/statistical Methods, results and study limitations; exact fresh PubMed date/status.
